title: MORABLES: A Benchmark for Assessing Abstract Moral Reasoning in LLMs with Fables

bias_targets.methodology: Introducing adversarial multiple-choice distractors, such as character swaps, similar-character morals, and trait injections, to evaluate whether models rely on superficial entity associations and shallow thematic matching rather than genuine moral reasoning.
Injecting adversarial tautologies at the beginning or end of the fables to observe if models are disproportionately influenced by initial or final tokens (i.e., 'attention sinks').

Analyzing answer selection distributions to investigate whether models disproportionately favor specific choice identifiers (e.g., letters like A, B, C or numbers like 1, 2, 3) regardless of the correct answer.

Comparing GPT-4o's performance to other models on the multiple-choice benchmark to ensure it did not have an unfair advantage, given that its own outputs were used to generate the dataset's distractor choices.
